title: DetectEntryPointReport
description:
Output ``data`` block for ``detect-entry-point`` (WS5 #4).

Wraps inside the standard SuccessEnvelope's ``data`` field (see
envelope.json). ``kind`` is ``greenfield`` when the scan found NO
entry-point candidate of any kind AND no ``@register_run`` on disk —
otherwise ``detected``. ``candidates`` carries one entry per discovered
entry point with its classified argv style; ``decoration_found`` lists
the files already carrying ``@register_run`` decoration. This is exactly
what ``hpc-wrap-entry-point`` SKILL.md branches on in Step 0 (scaffold
vs. onboard) and Step 1 (pick the entry point + its CLI surface).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: ``greenfield`` iff no entry-point candidate of any kind exists and no ``@register_run`` is on disk; else ``detected``. Step 0 scaffolds via ``build-template`` on ``greenfield`` and onboards the existing entry point on ``detected``.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: One entry per discovered entry-point candidate, in by-likelihood probe order. Python files carry their classified ``argv_kind`` (argparse / click / typer / hydra / fire / __main__); console scripts and shell/binary entry points carry ``console_script`` / ``shell``.

decoration_found.title: Decoration Found
decoration_found.description: Relative paths of files containing a ``@register_run`` decoration (the ``grep -rln '@register_run' notebooks/ src/ *.py`` probe). A non-empty list means the repo is already (partially) onboarded.

materialized.title: Materialized
materialized.description: The ``_materialized.entry_point`` block from ``interview.json`` when a wrapper-fallback onboarding (``hpc-wrap-entry-point``) already chose an entry point — ``null``/absent otherwise. Lets one ``detect-entry-point`` call answer submit.md Step 0b: branch on ``materialized.kind`` to honor a materialized wrapper, falling back to the ``candidates`` / ``decoration_found`` mature-repo probe when it is absent.

MaterializedEntryPoint.title: MaterializedEntryPoint
MaterializedEntryPoint.description: The worker-facing subset of ``interview.json``'s ``_materialized.entry_point`` block. ``kind`` selects the Step 0b procedure: ``shell_command`` and ``python_module`` short-circuit Step 1's discover scan (honor the materialized wrapper / dotted module; the per-task executor is ``executor_cmd``, which ``resolve-submit-inputs`` writes into the sidecar in code, feed ``data_axis`` into axes.yaml if present); ``register_run`` is a pointer that falls through to normal discovery. Only the fields the source block declares are present (the internal ``frozen_shas`` identity detail is intentionally omitted).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The materialized entry-point shape. ``shell_command``: a thin ``@register_run`` wrapper was materialized (the fallback path) — skip Step 1's discover scan. ``python_module``: an importable ``module``:``function`` targeted by dotted path — also skip discovery (no ``@register_run`` to find); its per-task executor is ``executor_cmd`` (a ``run-module`` dispatch). ``register_run``: a pointer to a decorated function the worker resolves through normal Step 1 discovery.

run_name.title: Run Name
run_name.description: The wrapper / run function name (``shell_command`` and ``register_run`` kinds). For ``shell_command`` this is the materialized ``.hpc/wrappers/<run_name>.py``; treat it as the picked run.

wrapper_path.title: Wrapper Path
wrapper_path.description: POSIX-relative path to the materialized ``@register_run`` wrapper (``shell_command`` kind only), e.g. ``.hpc/wrappers/<run_name>.py``.

executor_cmd.title: Executor Cmd
executor_cmd.description: The per-task executor command for this entry point (``shell_command``, ``register_run``, and ``python_module`` kinds). ``resolve-submit-inputs`` writes it into the sidecar's ``executor`` field deterministically from the materialized block, so the worker does not synthesize one from ``discover-executors`` or divine a ``python3 -m <module>`` (the ridge_imp exit-127 class).

module.title: Module
module.description: Dotted importable module path (``python_module`` kind only), e.g. ``my_pkg.train``.

function.title: Function
function.description: The function inside ``module`` to target (``python_module`` kind only).

data_axis.title: Data Axis
data_axis.description: Pre-declared series-axis classification (``shell_command`` kind, when the experimenter declared ``data_axis_hint``). When present, skip the Step 3b classification interview and feed this block into the axes.yaml write classify-axis would have done.

ArgvParam.title: ArgvParam
ArgvParam.description: One CLI parameter read MECHANICALLY off the candidate's AST (argparse ``add_argument`` / click ``@click.option`` + ``@click.argument``). Nothing here is inferred: every field is present only because the source states it as a literal, so the wrapper path can compose ``entry_point.argv`` + ``signature`` without the LLM re-typing flag names from an eyeballed read. When ONE written argument of this parameter is not modeled, the parameter is still emitted and ``unextracted`` NAMES it — a consumer composing an argv must treat any param carrying ``unextracted`` as an LLM leg (the verdict stays ``extracted`` because the parameter list is still complete in count and names).

names.title: Names
names.description: The declared name strings, in source order: option strings for a flag (``["--seed", "-s"]``) or the single name for a positional.

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: The attribute name the framework binds the value to — the explicit ``dest=`` when written, else the framework's own rule (argparse: first long option; click: the longest declared name), dashes converted to underscores.

positional.title: Positional
positional.description: ``true`` for a positional argument (an argparse name not starting with ``-``, or a ``@click.argument``); ``false`` for an option/flag.

type.title: Type
type.description: Source text of the written ``type=`` argument (``int``, ``float``, ``pathlib.Path``, a custom converter name). A STRING, never resolved — the framework does not import the user's module to learn what it names. Absent when no ``type=`` was written.

default.title: Default
default.description: The written ``default=`` value when it is a JSON-round-trippable literal. Absent when no default was written, or when the default is an expression (see ``default_source``).

default_source.title: Default Source
default_source.description: Source text of a written ``default=`` that is NOT a literal (``os.cpu_count()``, a module constant, …). Present instead of ``default`` so the caller sees that a default EXISTS without the framework pretending to know its value.

required.title: Required
required.description: The written ``required=`` literal. Absent when the source does not state it — the framework does not re-derive each library's implicit requiredness rules.

is_flag.title: Is Flag
is_flag.description: ``true`` when the parameter takes NO value (argparse ``action="store_true"``/``"store_false"``/``"count"``, click ``is_flag=True``, click ``count=True``, or a click boolean on/off pair like ``"--shout/--no-shout"``) — the wrapper argv appends the flag alone, never ``<flag> <value>``. Absent otherwise.

secondary_names.title: Secondary Names
secondary_names.description: The OFF side of a click boolean pair (``"--shout/--no-shout"`` → ``["--no-shout"]``). Present only for a pair, which is why it disambiguates a pair from plain aliases (``"--verbose", "-v"``) — both of which can carry ``is_flag``.

nargs.title: Nargs
nargs.description: The written ``nargs=`` literal — an integer (including click's ``-1`` variadic argument) or one of argparse's ``"+"`` / ``"*"`` / ``"?"``. Absent when not written; NAMED in ``unextracted`` when written as a non-literal expression (it changes the parameter's arity, so it is never dropped silently).

choices.title: Choices
choices.description: The written ``choices=`` literal sequence — the bounded value domain (a swept value outside it fails at parse time on the cluster). Absent when not written; NAMED in ``unextracted`` when written as a ``range`` / constant / other non-literal.

multiple.title: Multiple
multiple.description: ``true`` for click ``multiple=True`` — the option is repeatable and its values collect into a tuple, so one argv occurrence per value. Absent otherwise.

action.title: Action
action.description: The written argparse ``action=`` string, verbatim. ``store`` / ``store_true`` / ``store_false`` / ``count`` are fully modeled (the last three set ``is_flag``); any other literal action (``append``, ``extend``, ``store_const``, ``version``, …) is recorded here AND named in ``unextracted`` because its arity/repeat semantics are not modeled. A non-literal action (a custom Action class) yields no ``action`` field, only the ``unextracted`` entry.

unextracted.title: Unextracted
unextracted.description: Names of the written arguments this extractor did NOT model for this parameter (e.g. ``["action"]``, ``["nargs"]``, ``["count"]``, ``["dest"]``). Sorted, de-duplicated, and ABSENT when nothing was left unread. Present means: the parameter's names are real, but a consumer must read the source for the named argument(s) rather than compose blind — the ``compose_audit_template`` ``skipped`` posture (named, never silently dropped) applied per parameter.

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description: One entry-point candidate: its path (relative to the experiment dir, or the registered command name for a console script) plus the classified argv style, the mechanical parameter-extraction verdict, plus — when a known solver library was recognized in the source — the solver adapter that can checkpoint-instrument it.

path.title: Path
path.description: Path relative to the experiment dir (e.g. ``train.py``, ``src/main.py``, ``mypkg/__main__.py``), or — for a ``[project.scripts]`` console script — the registered command name.

argv_kind.title: Argv Kind
argv_kind.description: The candidate's CLI surface. Python files: ``argparse`` / ``click`` / ``typer`` / ``hydra`` / ``fire`` (by import + decorator), or ``__main__`` for a bare ``if __name__`` block or a package ``__main__.py`` with no recognized library. ``console_script`` for a ``[project.scripts]`` entry; ``shell`` for a non-Python ``run.sh`` / ``launch.sh`` / binary.

argv_extraction.title: Argv Extraction
argv_extraction.description: Whether this candidate's CLI parameters were read mechanically. ``extracted``: ``argv_params`` is the AST-read list (argparse / click — possibly EMPTY when the parser declares no flags). ``unsupported``: ``argv_params`` is ``null`` and the surface is not mechanically knowable — typer (params come from Python type hints), hydra (a composed YAML tree), fire (a live signature), a bare ``__main__``, a console script (opaque target), a shell/binary entry point, an unparseable file, or an argparse/click declaration that is not one flat local surface (parser built elsewhere, ``add_subparsers``, a click group of several commands). Keep the LLM leg for those; never guess.

argv_params.title: Argv Params
argv_params.description: The mechanically extracted CLI parameters when ``argv_extraction == "extracted"``, else ``null``. Ordered as declared in the source (argparse ``add_argument`` order; click decorator source order, which is the order click binds them).

solver.title: Solver
solver.description: Present when a known solver library's solve loop was detected in the candidate's source (AST match: petsc4py import + a PETSc.TS()/PETSc.SNES() construction + a .solve() call). Signals that the checkpoint-instrumented wrapper (``entry_point.solver`` on the interview intent) is available for this candidate — the library owns the iteration loop, so checkpointing injects via its monitor/options hooks rather than the executor loop helpers.
